metaData.originalTitle: The 10 best penalty takers at the 2026 World Cup (with apologies to Messi and Ronaldo)
metaData.title: The 10 best penalty takers at the 2026 World Cup (with apologies to Messi and Ronaldo)
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article ranks the top 10 penalty takers at the 2026 World Cup based on data-driven analysis and expert assessment, excluding Messi and Ronaldo due to below-average recent conversion rates.
metaData.summary: Geir Jordet, a soccer psychology expert, and his team compiled a dataset of 535 players' penalty records from official senior matches, filtering by conversion rate, volume, and other factors. The top 10 list prioritizes recent form, technical flexibility (goalkeeper-dependent vs. independent), and pressure performance. Notable entries include Harry Kane (1st) for his adaptive technique, Viktor Gyokeres (2nd) for pure power, and Raul Jimenez (3rd) for an astonishing 97.4% success rate. The article explains why global stars Messi (78%) and Ronaldo (declining 76.6%) are omitted, and provides deep tactical breakdowns for each player, including vulnerabilities.

mainPoints.point: Penalties are more critical than ever in the expanded 48-team World Cup.
mainPoints.explanation: The additional 16 knockout matches increase the probability of shootouts, making penalty proficiency a decisive factor.

mainPoints.point: The ranking is built on a rigorous data methodology and expert judgment.
mainPoints.explanation: The author's team analyzed 535 players from official senior matches, filtering by conversion rate, recent form, and psychological robustness, then added subjective factors like technique and stress coping.

mainPoints.point: Top takers exhibit technical flexibility and pressure management.
mainPoints.explanation: Players like Kane and Calhanoglu alternate between goalkeeper-dependent and independent techniques, while Mbappe's rapid style and composure in high-stakes situations (e.g., 2022 World Cup final) set him apart.

mainPoints.point: Messi and Ronaldo are excluded due to below-average recent conversion rates.
mainPoints.explanation: Despite career volume, Messi's 78% and Ronaldo's 76.6% over the last 30 kicks fall below the elite threshold, and both now play at lower club levels.
